key_insight: Zero-shot LLMs, especially Gemini 3.5 Flash, extracted colorectal cancer symptoms from discharge notes more accurately than rule-based or clinical NER methods.
clinical_relevance: This suggests LLM-based symptom surveillance could reduce manual chart review and improve scalable oncology NLP pipelines.
method: 2,704 MIMIC-IV colorectal cancer discharge notes analyzed
46 symptoms targeted from validated symptom inventories
Compared rule-based matching, pretrained clinical NER, and zero-shot Claude/Gemini models against a 200-note adjudicated gold standard
evidence_signal: Gemini 3.5 Flash achieved the best overall performance (Macro F1 0.70, Micro F1 0.86), outperforming rule-based and NER baselines on adjudicated evaluation.
watch_item: Post-hoc negation filtering reduced LLM performance, showing that fixed-window correction can override correct detections without syntactic scope handling.
paper_title: Leveraging Large Language Models for Colorectal Cancer Symptom Extraction from MIMIC-IV Clinical Notes
